# Weather Models (weathermodels.app)

> Weather Models compares nine global weather forecast models side by side, one row per day. Every cell shows the minimum, mean and maximum forecast across the models, so the spread between them is visible at a glance. Free, no account, nothing tracked; everything runs in the browser.

Models compared (via Open-Meteo, all keyless and open): ECMWF IFS, ECMWF AIFS (AI), NOAA GFS, DWD ICON, Met Office UKMO, Météo-France ARPEGE, ECCC GEM, JMA and CMA GRAPES. The "seamless" variants blend each agency's regional high-resolution model where one exists, so the same nine sources work anywhere in the world.

Columns (user-selectable and re-orderable, 23 available): high and low temperature, feels-like high and low, rain, chance of precipitation, wet hours, snow, wind, wind average, gusts, wind direction (circular mean), cloud cover, low, mid and high cloud (each the mean of the day's hours; GEM is left out because its layers do not match its own total), visibility (the day's lowest hour, from the four models that publish it: GFS, UKMO, CMA GRAPES and, over Europe, ICON; 20 km and over shows as 20+), humidity, dew point, pressure, sunshine hours, UV index and a "Sky" summary (the most common WMO weather code). Default view: High, Low, Rain, Chance, Wind, Sky.

Each day expands into hourly rows (or 3-hour blocks) with the same min/mean/max format. Hovering or tapping a cell lists every model's value, lowest to highest. Purple outer numbers flag disagreement between models. Small arrows on most number columns (temperatures, feels-like, rain, snow, wind, gusts, cloud, humidity, dew point, pressure and sunshine; not chance, UV, visibility or the cloud layers) show whether the models' mean for the day has moved since their forecast for it made three days ahead (or two, or one), using Open-Meteo's previous-runs archive; a model counts only on days both forecasts cover in full and its earlier one is not just a copy of its latest run, so only the next few days have an arrow. Times follow Open-Meteo's convention: one fixed UTC offset (the place's offset now) for the whole forecast, so after a clock change within the forecast they are an hour off local time, which the page notes under the place name.

Place search uses Photon (OpenStreetMap data) with Open-Meteo's geocoder as fallback; "Find me" uses the browser's location only when clicked. Privacy: the chosen coordinates are sent to Open-Meteo and the search text (or Find-me position) to Photon, all over HTTPS; nothing else leaves the browser and there are no cookies or analytics. Units switch between °C/km/h/mm and °F/mph/in.

Formerly meanweather.net ("Mean Weather"); renamed 2026-10-06, and the old address redirects here.

Technical: static files only (the forecast table: index.html, style.css, app.js; the accuracy page: most-accurate-weather-forecast/, accuracy.js, accuracy.css), MIT-licensed, no build step, no backend, no analytics. Forecast data © Open-Meteo (CC BY 4.0); place data © OpenStreetMap contributors.

## Links

- [Forecast table](https://weathermodels.app/): the app itself
- [Which weather forecast is most accurate where you are](https://weathermodels.app/most-accurate-weather-forecast/): league table of the nine models for any place, scored in the browser against ERA5 reanalysis (daily high and low error, warm/cold bias, wet/dry calls on 1 mm or more of precipitation, snow counted as melted water; a day counts only when all its hours are there) for forecasts made 1, 2, 3, 5 or 7 days ahead (per hour: each hour comes from the run made that long before it) over the last 30 or 90 days, with a "too close to call" test; ERA5 lags about five days, so the period ends roughly a week ago. Pre-rendered examples for London, New York and Sydney. Same `?at=lat,lon&n=` links, plus `lead=`, `days=` and `by=temp|hi|lo|rain`
- [Shareable view](https://weathermodels.app/?at=51.5074,-0.1278&n=London): `?at=lat,lon` opens a place directly; optional `n=` (name), `cols=` (comma-separated column keys), `off=` (model ids switched off), `units=imperial`, `step=1`, `avg=median`, `tmp=1` (show without remembering)
